column1: # Acceptance of ADR-003's rules (011 WI-4) at ce9cb247: predictions, written before any run.
# Source: HANDOFF-accept-judge-recoveries.md, "The rows", and PLAN-judge-recoveries-on-real-runs.md WI-4.
# This file is hashed (predictions.tsv.sha256) and the hash is the first line of sequence.log.
# It is not edited after that. A prediction that turns out wrong is a prediction miss in mutants.tsv.
# Members (16), as `JUDGE` labels: seed-1 seed-2 seed-4 seed-5 seed-7 seed-9 seed-10 seed-12 seed-15
#   seed-19 seed-30 seed-32 seed-62 seed-141 seed-244 constructed-empty-terminal
# OK10      = seed-1 seed-2 seed-4 seed-9 seed-10 seed-12 seed-15 seed-62 seed-141 constructed-empty-terminal
# PROVFAIL5 = seed-5 seed-7 seed-19 seed-30 seed-32
# DISPATCH10= seed-1 seed-4 seed-10 seed-12 seed-15 seed-19 seed-32 seed-62 seed-141 seed-244
#  S1. A row is a KILL when the gate's output holds `JUDGE <member> <rule id> RED` for the rule id
#      in `expect_red`, on at least one bank member. `CONTROL` and `SELFCHECK` rows do not count.
#  S2. Where `direction` is not `-`, that text must open the row's detail (`RED <direction>:`).
#      The rule red in the other direction only is NOT a kill of the case the row names.
#      Row r09's direction is this file's own reading, not the handoff's: there a different
#      direction is a prediction miss and not a lost kill.
#  S3. A row naming two rule ids (r09) is a kill when both are red; each id is also scored alone.
#  S4. A compile or type error, a timeout, a non-zero exit with no row for the named rule, or
#      another rule red alone is NOT a kill and is recorded as what it is. Exit status is not read
#  S5. `members` is the predicted set of members with the named rule red. A different set with
#      the rule red is a kill and a prediction miss. `count:12` predicts a count and no names.
#  S6. `also` is what else is predicted to go red. It does not decide the kill. `none` predicts
#      that no other rule id is red on any member; anything else red is a prediction miss.
#  S7. A control row passes on its `expect` text; a control that does not is a stop-and-report.
